summary: charge_confusion_rate.py control mode accepted an MC control sample of the other true sign, or of both signs pooled, so the data/MC scale factor silently compared different species.

observables: control-mode scale_factor and mc rate per bin
impact.bias: an MC sample of the other sign gave e.g. a scale factor 0.069 instead of the same-species value; pooled signs gave an MC rate of 0.0166 against 0.0010 for the data's species (c+ and c- differ), with status ok and no warning
impact.trigger: control mode with --mc whose true-sign column holds the other sign or both signs

outputs.how_to_recognize: JSON on stdout of charge_confusion_rate.py control with --mc: bins[].mc and scale_factor; the MC file's true-sign column shows whether it held other signs; no artifact records the run

remedy: check the true signs of the MC control samples used; rerun with an MC sample of the data's true sign only (a mixed file must be split by true sign) on a version with the fix
